input.command:
D=/scr/wurgaft/auto-psych/agent_trees/8a52ff3d6e8e6ef7/repo/_runs/cell_1/experiment3/model_loop/iter_4/critique/test_stats
mkdir -p $D && rm -f $D/*.py
HELP='def _feat(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True)
    s = s.apply(lambda c: pd.to_numeric(c, errors="coerce"))
    a = s.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(a), axis=1)
    mn = np.nanmin(a, axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(a, axis=1)
    is_ex = np.any(a == t[:, None], axis=1)
    par = np.where(np.isnan(a), np.nan, np.mod(a, 2))
    allodd = np.nansum(par == 1, axis=1) == n
    alleven = np.nansum(par == 0, axis=1) == n
    return t, y, n, mn, mx, is_ex, allodd, alleven

def _m(y, mask):
    return float(np.mean(y[mask])) if np.any(mask) else 0.0
'
w(){ printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n%s\n' "# name: $1" "# description: $2" "$HELP" "$3" > $D/$1.py; }

w far_minus_near_above_range_gradient "Among targets above the set maximum, yes-rate for targets >30 above max minus yes-rate for targets 1-10 above max; observed > model means people extend upward generalization farther (flatter decay) than the model." 'def test_statistic(df):
    t, y, n, mn, mx, ex, ao, ae = _feat(df)
    d = t - mx
    return _m(y, d > 30) - _m(y, (d >= 1) & (d <= 10))'

w four_example_above_minus_below_range "For 4-example sets, yes-rate on targets above the max minus yes-rate on targets below the min; observed > model means a stronger upward asymmetry than the model predicts." 'def test_statistic(df):
    t, y, n, mn, mx, ex, ao, ae = _feat(df)
    k = n == 4
    return _m(y, k & (t > mx)) - _m(y, k & (t < mn))'

w mixed_parity_set_in_minus_out_range "For sets of >=2 examples with mixed parity, yes-rate on non-example targets inside [min,max] minus yes-rate outside; observed > model means people rely more on magnitude range for mixed-parity sets than the model." 'def test_statistic(df):
    t, y, n, mn, mx, ex, ao, ae = _feat(df)
    k = (n >= 2) & ~ao & ~ae & ~ex
    inr = (t >= mn) & (t <= mx)
    return _m(y, k & inr) - _m(y, k & ~inr)'

w same_parity_set_opposite_parity_rate "For sets of >=2 examples all of one parity, yes-rate on in-range targets of the opposite parity; observed > model means people enforce parity less strictly than the model (model over-sharpens parity)." 'def test_statistic(df):
    t, y, n, mn, mx, ex, ao, ae = _feat(df)
    tp = np.mod(t, 2)
    opp = (ao & (tp == 0)) | (ae & (tp == 1))
    k = (n >= 2) & opp & (t >= mn) & (t <= mx)
    return _m(y, k)'

w set_level_sd_nonexample_rate "Standard deviation across number sets of the per-set yes-rate on non-example targets; observed > model means sets differ more sharply in breadth of generalization than the model produces." 'def test_statistic(df):
    t, y, n, mn, mx, ex, ao, ae = _feat(df)
    k = ~ex
    if not np.any(k):
        return 0.0
    g = pd.Series(y[k]).groupby(df["number_set"].astype(str).to_numpy()[k]).mean()
    return float(g.std(ddof=0)) if len(g) > 1 else 0.0'

w single_example_below_rate "For single-example sets, yes-rate on targets below the example; observed > model means people generalize downward from one example more than the model predicts." 'def test_statistic(df):
    t, y, n, mn, mx, ex, ao, ae = _feat(df)
    return _m(y, (n == 1) & (t < mn))'

w two_example_out_of_range_rate "For two-example sets, yes-rate on targets outside [min,max]; observed > model means people generalize beyond the examples range more than the model with two examples." 'def test_statistic(df):
    t, y, n, mn, mx, ex, ao, ae = _feat(df)
    return _m(y, (n == 2) & ((t < mn) | (t > mx)))'

w wide_minus_mid_span_in_range "For sets with >=2 examples, in-range non-example yes-rate when span>=50 minus when span is 15-49; observed > model means wide-span sets are filled in more relative to mid spans than the model predicts." 'def test_statistic(df):
    t, y, n, mn, mx, ex, ao, ae = _feat(df)
    sp = mx - mn
    k = (n >= 2) & ~ex & (t >= mn) & (t <= mx)
    return _m(y, k & (sp >= 50)) - _m(y, k & (sp >= 15) & (sp < 50))'
cd /tmp && python3 -c "

"; grep -l import $D/*.py

HELP='def _feat(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True)
    s = s.apply(lambda c: pd.to_numeric(c, errors="coerce"))
    a = s.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(a), axis=1)
    mn = np.nanmin(a, axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(a, axis=1)
    is_ex = np.any(a == t[:, None], axis=1)
    par = np.where(np.isnan(a), np.nan, np.mod(a, 2))
    allodd = np.nansum(par == 1, axis=1) == n
    alleven = np.nansum(par == 0, axis=1) == n
    return t, y, n, mn, mx, is_ex, allodd, alleven

def _m(y, mask):
    return float(np.mean(y[mask])) if np.any(mask) else 0.0
'
w(){ printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n%s\n' "# name: $1" "# description: $2" "$HELP" "$3" > $D/$1.py; }

w far_minus_near_above_range_gradient "Among targets above the set maximum, yes-rate for targets >30 above max minus yes-rate for targets 1-10 above max; observed > model means people extend upward generalization farther (flatter decay) than the model." 'def test_statistic(df):
    t, y, n, mn, mx, ex, ao, ae = _feat(df)
    d = t - mx
    return _m(y, d > 30) - _m(y, (d >= 1) & (d <= 10))'

w four_example_above_minus_below_range "For 4-example sets, yes-rate on targets above the max minus yes-rate on targets below the min; observed > model means a stronger upward asymmetry than the model predicts." 'def test_statistic(df):
    t, y, n, mn, mx, ex, ao, ae = _feat(df)
    k = n == 4
    return _m(y, k & (t > mx)) - _m(y, k & (t < mn))'

w mixed_parity_set_in_minus_out_range "For sets of >=2 examples with mixed parity, yes-rate on non-example targets inside [min,max] minus yes-rate outside; observed > model means people rely more on magnitude range for mixed-parity sets than the model." 'def test_statistic(df):
    t, y, n, mn, mx, ex, ao, ae = _feat(df)
    k = (n >= 2) & ~ao & ~ae & ~ex
    inr = (t >= mn) & (t <= mx)
    return _m(y, k & inr) - _m(y, k & ~inr)'

w same_parity_set_opposite_parity_rate "For sets of >=2 examples all of one parity, yes-rate on in-range targets of the opposite parity; observed > model means people enforce parity less strictly than the model (model over-sharpens parity)." 'def test_statistic(df):
    t, y, n, mn, mx, ex, ao, ae = _feat(df)
    tp = np.mod(t, 2)
    opp = (ao & (tp == 0)) | (ae & (tp == 1))
    k = (n >= 2) & opp & (t >= mn) & (t <= mx)
    return _m(y, k)'

w set_level_sd_nonexample_rate "Standard deviation across number sets of the per-set yes-rate on non-example targets; observed > model means sets differ more sharply in breadth of generalization than the model produces." 'def test_statistic(df):
    t, y, n, mn, mx, ex, ao, ae = _feat(df)
    k = ~ex
    if not np.any(k):
        return 0.0
    g = pd.Series(y[k]).groupby(df["number_set"].astype(str).to_numpy()[k]).mean()
    return float(g.std(ddof=0)) if len(g) > 1 else 0.0'

w single_example_below_rate "For single-example sets, yes-rate on targets below the example; observed > model means people generalize downward from one example more than the model predicts." 'def test_statistic(df):
    t, y, n, mn, mx, ex, ao, ae = _feat(df)
    return _m(y, (n == 1) & (t < mn))'

w two_example_out_of_range_rate "For two-example sets, yes-rate on targets outside [min,max]; observed > model means people generalize beyond the examples range more than the model with two examples." 'def test_statistic(df):
    t, y, n, mn, mx, ex, ao, ae = _feat(df)
    return _m(y, (n == 2) & ((t < mn) | (t > mx)))'

w wide_minus_mid_span_in_range "For sets with >=2 examples, in-range non-example yes-rate when span>=50 minus when span is 15-49; observed > model means wide-span sets are filled in more relative to mid spans than the model predicts." 'def test_statistic(df):
    t, y, n, mn, mx, ex, ao, ae = _feat(df)
    sp = mx - mn
    k = (n >= 2) & ~ex & (t >= mn) & (t <= mx)
    return _m(y, k & (sp >= 50)) - _m(y, k & (sp >= 15) & (sp < 50))'
cd /tmp && python3 -c "

for f in sorted(glob.glob('$D/*.py')):

"; grep -l import $D/*.py
